name: PowerInfer: Fast Large Language Model Inference with a Consumer-grade GPU
problem: A consumer PC has a GPU with far less memory and bandwidth than a datacenter GPU, so an LLM that fits nowhere must either spill to CPU (PCIe-bound, very slow) or be shrunk to a lower-quality model; neither is acceptable if you want datacenter-class quality on commodity hardware.
mechanism: Exploits the power-law distribution of neuron activation: a small set of 'hot' neurons is consistently activated across inputs while the rest are input-dependent 'cold' neurons. Hot neurons are kept resident on the GPU with FP16 weights; cold neurons are handled on the CPU with lighter precision. A neuron-outlier predictor decides hot/cold placement ahead of execution, and request batching is made proactive because placement quality depends on request composition.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim: up to 7.1x higher throughput than a standard framework (FlexGen) on the same consumer GPU at comparable latency; a llama.cpp-derived baseline is also beaten. See also the PowerInfer-2 follow-up (arXiv 2406.06282) for the smartphone result - a different paper, not this record.
notes: Added for the commodity-hardware end of the serving story: the repo's serving records (pagedattention-vllm, distserve, splitwise, orca-osdi22-iteration-scheduling) all assume a datacentre GPU fleet.
